title: Mathlib Imports
content: Imports SimpleGraph.Basic for graph adjacency, Nat.Basic and Finset.Basic for arithmetic and finite sets, Order.Filter.Basic for asymptotic notation, and general tactics. The filter import supports the asymptotic bounds ($\gg$ and $\ll$) central to the problem statement.
mathContext: Requires $\text{SimpleGraph}$ for graph structure, $\text{Fin}\,n$ for vertex sets, and $\text{Filter}$ for asymptotic growth comparisons.

title: Cycle Containment
content: HasCycleOfLength G n holds when G contains a cycle of length $n$: there exist $n$ distinct vertices $v_0, v_1, \ldots, v_{n-1}$ such that $v_i$ and $v_{(i+1) \bmod n}$ are adjacent for all $i$. The constraint $n \geq 2$ excludes degenerate cases. The definition uses Function.Injective to ensure all vertices are distinct, which is the key combinatorial constraint.
mathContext: $\text{HasCycleOfLength}(G, n) \iff \exists v : \text{Fin}\,n \hookrightarrow V,\; \forall i,\; G.\text{Adj}(v_i, v_{i+1 \bmod n})$ with $n \geq 2$

title: Edge Colorings and Monochromatic Subgraphs
content: EdgeColoring m k is a function $\text{Fin}\,m \to \text{Fin}\,m \to \text{Fin}\,k$ assigning one of $k$ colors to each pair. monochromaticGraph $\chi$ $c$ extracts the subgraph of edges colored $c$, verified as a SimpleGraph (symmetric, irreflexive). The symmetry proof has a sorry for the coloring symmetry assumption $\chi(u,v) = \chi(v,u)$. This is the multicolor generalization of 2-colorings used in classical Ramsey theory.

title: Ramsey Number $R(C_{2n}; k)$
content: ramseyEvenCycle n k is $R(C_{2n}; k)$, the minimum $m$ such that every $k$-coloring of $K_m$ contains a monochromatic copy of the even cycle $C_{2n}$. Defined via Nat.find with a trivial existence witness. This multicolor Ramsey number is the central object of Problem 555: determining its exact growth rate as a function of $k$ for fixed $n$.
mathContext: $R(C_{2n}; k) = \min\{m : \forall \chi \text{ (k-coloring of } K_m),\; \exists c,\; C_{2n} \subseteq G_c\}$

title: Erdos General Bounds
content: Two axioms capture Erdos's bounds on $R(C_{2n}; k)$. The lower bound $R(C_{2n}; k) \gg k^{1+1/(2n)}$ comes from probabilistic or algebraic constructions: for $C_4$, the construction uses polarity graphs of finite projective planes. The upper bound $R(C_{2n}; k) \ll k^{1+1/(n-1)}$ (for $n \geq 2$) uses Szemeredi regularity or dependent random choice to find long paths in dense monochromatic subgraphs. The gap between exponents $1/(2n)$ and $1/(n-1)$ is the central open question.
mathContext: $\exists c > 0,\; c \cdot k^{1+1/(2n)} \leq R(C_{2n}; k)$; $\exists C > 0,\; R(C_{2n}; k) \leq C \cdot k^{1+1/(n-1)}$
